To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a global road dataset with 21 million km and that we have used this dataset to estimate that the world's total road length will grow from about 50 million km to 55–58 million km by the year 2055, with the largest increases in the world's remaining wilderness areas.
the Global Roads Inventory dataset is the first global road map with high spatial coverage and accuracy.
we developed a new global roads dataset, which includes more roads and is more complete than existing road datasets, and that we used this dataset to project future road infrastructure in 2050.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the global patterns of current and expected road infrastructure, and the implications of these patterns on spatial planning, socio-economics and the environment.
the spatial patterns of current and predicted future road infrastructure, and how they relate to socio-economic and environmental variables.
the development of an improved, harmonized global roads dataset and the use of this dataset to estimate future trends in road length.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the global road infrastructure is increasing and the increase will be most prominent in the developing countries.
the current road network is highly biased towards developed countries and is expected to expand rapidly in developing countries.
the current road infrastructure in most developing countries is insufficient to meet the needs for future economic development, while in many developed countries it is excessive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Global Roads Inventory dataset provides a valuable resource for global and regional assessments of road infrastructure.
the current global road network is dominated by developed nations and that the projected increase in global road length will likely occur in the world's remaining pristine wilderness areas.
we provide the most comprehensive, up-to-date and spatially explicit global road dataset, and that we provide an estimate of future global road length based on the SSP scenarios.
The main takeaway from our work is that
road infrastructure is an important component of human well-being, and its expansion is likely to continue, but that the expansion is not uniform across the world.

global road infrastructure data is now available at a much higher spatial resolution, with a more comprehensive global coverage, and that the road infrastructure of the future will be much more extensive.
global road maps can be improved by integrating existing road datasets, which can be used to improve spatial planning and to assess the impact of roads on biodiversity and human health.
